thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH latency alert for /v1/stream (p95/p99 breach). p95 jumped from ~420ms to ~2.1s, p99 from ~1.1s to ~4.8s at 2026-03-14T14:03:54Z. Error rate on control-plane DB calls spiked.

mike: acked. I'm the on-call Eng. Paging SRE and runtime. Starting triage — grabbing logs and top traces.

sara: seeing streaming stalls and reconnects in the logs. Clients show stalled chunks then reconnects. Tail queues backing up on the runtime side.

raj: I'm SRE, on it. Initial look at control-plane DB shows connection saturation and occasional "ERROR: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser" and repeated auth timeouts. Also seeing long latencies from config-fetch RPCs to config-service (~600ms -> 2s).

mike: that matches what I see. Reconstruction: inference path calls control-plane for per-request feature flags/config + auth check. If DB and config-service stall, we add ~1s tail latency per request. Streaming amplifies since prefix cache misses cause repeated fetches.

emily: what's customer impact? any enterprise SLAs at risk? Which tenants hit error spikes?

jordan: support reports two customers (acme-inc, finlytics) filing errors in last 10m complaining about long responses and reconnect loops for streaming. We've also had a few automated pager escalations from premium routes.

raj: mitigation plan (short):
- 1) Disable dynamic per-request config fetch (flip feature flag) to fall back to cached config for all requests
- 2) Temporarily increase DB max_connections for control-plane and bump app pool size to absorb backlog
- 3) Route streaming to reserve capacity pool if available or fallback model variant that needs fewer control-plane lookups
- 4) Monitor p95/p99 and error rates, rollback if regression

mike: agree. Disabling dynamic config is lowest-risk and fastest. Preparing flag toggle now. Command (internal FF service):
```
POST https://ff.internal/api/toggle
{"flag":"use_dynamic_config","value":false,"scope":"global","actor":"mike"}
```

ops-bot: :gear: Feature flag "use_dynamic_config" set to false (canary 0->100%) by mike at 2026-03-14T14:08:02Z.

raj: also increased DB max_connections from 200 -> 350 on control-plane DB (temp). Command: `ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = '350';` followed by a rolling restart of the config-service pods.

sara: after flag toggle and restart: streaming stalls dropped a lot on canary. Observed cache hit rate for config-service jump from 68% -> 97% and tail latencies decreased.

mike: pushing rollout to 100% traffic. Watching metrics.

ops-bot: Canary success: 10%->100% rollout completed at 2026-03-14T14:12:30Z.

raj: live metrics update: p95 down to ~480ms, p99 down to ~1.4s, error rate for streaming routes back to baseline. DB connection queue elongated briefly but drained after pool bump.

emily: good. For customer communications: we need a short blurb describing impact and mitigation. Draft: "We observed increased latency and streaming stalls affecting some customers due to a burst of control-plane DB load. We temporarily disabled dynamic per-request config fetch and increased DB pool size; service latency returned to normal. Engineering continues root-cause analysis and will follow up with a timeline and postmortem." Thoughts?

jordan: that's fine. I'll send to the two impacted customers and post status update to status.redwood.ai.

mike: documenting immediate actions in incident tracker. Current status: mitigated, partial rollback not needed. Next steps:
- Deep dive on what caused DB connection storm (traffic pattern? bad query? bug in config-service caching?)
- Re-evaluate config-service connection pooling and circuit-breakers
- Postmortem and timeline

raj: I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours then hand off. If anything regresses, page me immediately.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged by mike, severity -> SEV2. Auto-create incident ticket: INC-2026-0314-42. Postmortem requested within 72 hours.

mike: handing off to raj for ongoing monitoring. I'm available if we need code changes. Next on-call is sara (eng-runtime) starting 14:30 UTC; raj will maintain pager until handoff.

sara: taking handoff at 14:30. I'll follow up with an ops runbook entry for disabling dynamic config and the DB pool steps.

ops-bot: Reminder: create postmortem doc and link incident ticket in the doc.

emily: assign customer liaison for the postmortem; product will need the RCA before next exec sync.

mike: thanks everyone. Closing the urgent thread; moving conversation to the postmortem doc and RFC for config-service hardening.

(reacts :thumbsup: from many)
